children: The €40 bln carmaker struck a deal with its unions to slash 50,000 jobs and cut spending. The outcome of the tense negotiations is better than expected. But details like cost and timing are murky, and CEO Oliver Blume still needs EU lawmakers to fend off Chinese competition.
Volkswagen’s supervisory board on September 3 struck a turnaround agreement that includes sweeping job cuts.
The deal on the biggest restructuring in the group's 89-year history includes a further 50,000 job cuts, bringing the total agreed to 100,000, and leaves open the future of four of its German plants.

Volkswagen CEO Oliver Blume also said no new car models would be built in Emden, Zwickau, Hanover and Neckarsulm plants unless costs could be brought down. He is targeting a 9% operating margin target by 2030.
Shares in Volkswagen were up 5.32% by 0850 GMT on September 4.
